div.head: Rect 4.a, 4.1, 4.1a, 4.1b, 4.1c, 4.2, 4.2a, 4.2b. 4.2c
div.ab: [4.a] On sumen lande is, þæt he sceal wyrcan to wicweorce II dagas swilc weorc, swilc him man tæcð, ofer geares fyrst ælcre wucan, 7 on hærfest III dagas to wicweorce 7 of Candelmæsse oð Eastran III; gif he aferað, ne ðearf he wyrcan ða hwile ðe his hors ute bið. [4.1] He sceal syllan on Michaeles mæssedæig X gafolp'. 7 on Martinus mæssedæg XXIII systra beres 7 II henfugelas, on Eastran an geong sceap oððe II p. [4.1a] 7 he sceal licgan of Martinus mæssan oð Eastran æt hlafordes falde swa oft swa him to begæð. [4.1b] 7 of ðam timan, ðe man ærest ereð, oð Martinus mæssan he sceal ælcre wucan erian I æcer 7 ræcan sylf þæt sæd on hlafordes berne; [4.1c] toeacan ðam III æceras to bene 7 II to gærsyrðe; gyf he maran gærses beðyrfe, ðonne earnige ðæs, swa him man ðafige; [4.2] his gauolyrðe III æceras erige 7 sawe of his aganum berne. [4.2a] 7 sylle his heorðpænig. [4.2b] 7 twegen 7 twegen fedan ænne headorhund. [4.2c] 7 ælc gebur sylle VI hlafas ðam inswa[ne], ðonne he his heorde to mæstene drife.

[4a] In quibusdam terris operatur opus septimane duos dies sic opus, sicut ei dicetur, per anni spatium omni septimana, et in Augusto III dies pro septimanali operatione et a festo Candelarum adusque Pascha III; si aueriat, non cogitur operari, quamdiu equus eius foris moratur. [4.1] Dare debet in festo sancti Michaelis X d. de gablo et sancti Martini die XXIII et sestarium ordei et II gallinas, ad Pascha I ouem iuuenem uel II d. [4.1a] Et iacebit a festo sancti Martini usque ad Pascha ad faldam domini sui, quotiens ei pertinebit. [4.1b] Et a termino, quo primitus arabitur, usque ad festum sancti Martini arabit unaquaque septimana I acram et ipse parabit semen in horreo domini sui; [4.1c] ad hęc III acras precum et II de herbagio; si plus indigeat herbagio, arabit proinde, sicut ei permittetur. [4.2] De aratura gabli sui arabit III acras et seminabit de horreo suo. [4.2a] Et dabit suum heorðpenig. [4.2b] Et duo et duo pascant unum molossum. [4.2c] Et omnis geburus det VI panes porcario curie, quando gregem suum minabit in pastinagium.

In some estates [the custom] is that he must work [for] two days in each week, [doing] such work as he is directed to, throughout the year, and to work [for] three days each week during the harvest, and for three [days each week] from Candlemas to Easter. If he supplies horses for team-work, he need not work while his horses are out. He must pay ten pennies tax on Michaelmas day, and on the day of Martin’s Mass [he must give] twenty-three sesters of barley, and two hens; at Easter [he must give] a young sheep or two pennies. And from Martin’s Mass to Easter he must remain with the lord’s fold as often as it comes around to him. And from the time when one first ploughs to Martin’s Mass he must plough one acre each week, and collect the seed himself from the lord’s barn. In addition to that, [he must plough] three acres as compulsory service on demand and two [acres] pasturage-ploughing. If he needs more grass then he may earn it in such way as one allows him to. His plough-rent [is] to plough three acres and to sow [it with seed] from his own barn. And [he] pays his hearth-penny. As one of a pair [he must] feed a hunting dog. And each peasant pays six loaves to the lord’s swineherd when he drives his drove [of pigs] to woodland-pasture.

[4a] Auf manchem Landgut gilt, dass er über den [ganzen] Jahreslauf hin in jeder Woche zwei Tage als Wochenfrohn solche Arbeit, wie ihm zugewiesen wird, leisten muss; und in der Ernte drei Tage als Wochenfrohn; und von Lichtmess [2. Februar] bis Ostern drei; wenn er Spanndienst [für die Herrschaft] leistet, braucht er die Zeit, da sein Pferd draussen ist, nicht zu arbeiten. [4.1] Er muss an Michaelis Festtag [29. Sept.] 10 Zinspfennig zahlen und an Martinus' Festtag 23 [lies 24?] Sextar Gerste und zwei Hennen, zu Ostern ein Jungschaf oder 2 Pfennig. [4.1a] Und er muss von Martinus' Fest bis Ostern bei des Herrn [Vieh]hürde [als Wächter] liegen, so oft wie [die Reihe] an ihn kommt. [4.1b] Und von der Zeit an, da man zuerst [im Herbst] pflügt, bis Martinus' Fest muss er in jeder Woche 1 Acker pflügen [für die Herrschaft] und [dazu] das Saatkorn selbst in des Herrn Scheune erholen; [4.1c] ausserdem 3 Äcker [pflügen] als ‘Geheissarbeit’ [boonwork] und 2 als Heu[entgelt]-Pflügen; wenn er weiteren Heus bedarf, dann verdiene er dies, wie man [die Herrschaft] ihm verstattet. [4.2] Als sein Pachtpflügen pflüge er 3 Äcker und besäe [sie] aus seiner eigenen Scheune. [4.2a] Und er zahle seinen Herdpfennig. [4.2b] Und je zwei und zwei [Bauern] müssen einen Hochjagdhund füttern. [4.2c] Und jeder Bauer gebe sechs Laib Brot dem Domänen-Schweinehirten, wenn dieser seine Herde zur Mast treibt.

[4a] On some estates it holds that he must do two days' week-work each week throughout the [whole] year, such work as is assigned him; and three days' week-work at harvest; and three from Candlemas [2 February] to Easter; if he does carrying service [for the lord], he need not work while his horse is out. [4.1] He must pay 10 rent-pence on Michaelmas [29 September], and at Martinmas 23 [read 24?] sesters of barley and two hens, and at Easter a young sheep or 2 pence. [4.1a] And from Martinmas to Easter he must lie at the lord's [cattle-]fold [as watchman] as often as [his turn] comes. [4.1b] And from the time when ploughing first begins [in autumn] until Martinmas he must plough 1 acre each week [for the lord] and himself fetch the seed from the lord's barn; [4.1c] besides that, [plough] 3 acres as boon-work and 2 as grass-[rent] ploughing; if he needs more grass, let him earn it as [the lord] allows him. [4.2] As his rent-ploughing let him plough 3 acres and sow [them] from his own barn. [4.2a] And let him pay his hearth-penny. [4.2b] And every two [geburs] must feed one hunting-hound. [4.2c] And let every gebur give six loaves to the lord's swineherd when he drives his herd to the mast.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 4a–4.2c. Liebermann would correct ‘XXIII’ to ‘XXIIII’ (preference for multiples of twelve; the last I in the archetype probably resembled ⁊, which B read as a deletion and the Quadripartitus as ‘et’). B's ‘ræcan’ was unclearly altered in chalk to ‘ræfan’ or ‘ræpan’ (not, as editors read, ‘rædan’). Thorpe alters ‘erige’ following the Quadripartitus, wrongly given the genitive. The ‘7’ before ‘twegen’ was later erased. B reads ‘inswa’; Liebermann prints ‘inswa[ne]’. K: double spaces removed.
